correctness.rationale: The Hermitian first-sublattice operator has simple explicit sine-mode eigenvectors; nonvanishing lossy coupling eliminates real eigenvalues. The fixed-dimension Schur complement gives positive modal decay rates and exact normalized sitewise branching ratios in the strong-loss limit. Pairwise trigonometric reflection gives weighted mirror reciprocity. For linear losses the denominator is half the harmonic number times a positive trigonometric coefficient in the interior. The uniform trigonometric lower bound controls endpoint modes, giving a rigorous Riemann limit with the stated integral. Independent finite Lyapunov and eigenbasis computations reproduce the formulas; the general claim rests on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Material examination of the graded-loss 2022 primary paper and the uniform-loss 2020 and 2023 accounts identified the nearest phenomena and resolvent framework, but not the all-positive-weight strong-loss distribution, reciprocal-loss mirror identity, or logarithmic endpoint coefficient. This is a specific new evaluation within a known physical model, not an asserted new general adiabatic-elimination technique.
residual_risks: A separate unlocated specialist treatment of graded-loss adiabatic elimination could conceivably include an equivalent evaluated channel identity.

value.rationale: The anomalous far-end escape in a graded absorbing lattice is a motivated puzzle from the 2022 numerical study. The theorem predicts a striking exact inverse-weight pairwise boundary relation for arbitrary positive loss gradients and any injection site, plus a sharp long-chain logarithmic escape law for the linear profile and a coupling-dependent explicit coefficient. The statements have clear operational interpretations as integrated jump probabilities and distinguish strong absorption from an ordinary instantaneous localization effect.
